'''Louis Joseph Billera''' is a Professor of [[Mathematics]] at [[Cornell University]].

==Career==
Billera completed his B.S. at the [[Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute]] in 1964. He earned his Ph.D. from the [[Graduate Center of the City University of New York]] in 1968, under the joint supervision of Moses Richardson and [[Michel Balinski]].<ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=26980}}</ref>

Louis Billera served as the first Associate Director of the [[National Science Foundation]] [[DIMACS|Center for Discrete Mathematics and Theoretical Computer Science]] (DIMACS) at [[Rutgers University]].

In 2010 he gave the invited lecture, "''Flag enumeration in polytopes, Eulerian partially ordered sets and Coxeter groups''" at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in [[Hyderabad]].<ref>{{cite web|title=ICM Plenary and Invited Speakers since 1897|url=http://www.mathunion.org/db/ICM/Speakers/SortedByCongress.php|publisher=[[International Congress of Mathematicians]]|access-date=2013-08-14|archive-date=2017-11-08|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171108012153/http://www.mathunion.org/db/ICM/Speakers/SortedByCongress.php|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Contributions==
The common thread through much of his research is to study problems motivated by [[Discrete geometry|discrete]] and [[convex geometry]]. A sampling includes constructing [[polytope]]s to prove the sufficiency condition for the [[Simplicial sphere|g-theorem]] (with Carl Lee), discovering fiber polytopes (with [[Bernd Sturmfels]]), and studying the space of [[phylogenetic tree]]s (with [[Susan P. Holmes|Susan Holmes]] and [[Karen Vogtmann]]).

==Awards and honors==
In 1994 Billera won the [[Fulkerson Prize]] for his paper, ''Homology of smooth splines''. This prize is given every three years to the best paper in [[discrete mathematics]].<ref>{{cite web|title=American Mathematical Society Fulkerson Prize in Discrete Mathematics|url=https://www.ams.org/profession/prizes-awards/ams-prizes/fulkerson-prize}}</ref>

In 2012 he became a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>[https://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society], retrieved 2013-07-07.</ref>

==Selected publications==
*Louis Billera, "Homology of smooth splines: Generic triangulations and a conjecture of Strang", [[Transactions of the American Mathematical Society]] '''310''' (1988). 325&ndash;340.
*Louis Billera, [[Anders Björner]], [[Curtis Greene]], [[Rodica Simion]], [[Richard P. Stanley]] (eds.): New Perspectives in Algebraic Combinatorics, MSRI Publications, Cambridge University Press 1999, http://library.msri.org/books/Book38/
